prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Bypassing onboarding steps directly (new_flow) significantly improves conversion.
Reordering friction by moving sign-in after pet selection (reorder) significantly improves conversion.
Major redesigns (redesign) and sign-in hints (hint) significantly hurt performance.
Copy updates, permission checks, layout changes, and notifications showed no clear effect.
Predictions consistently overestimated actual measured gains across tests.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: +10.4% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, copy: +0.7% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, layout: -0.2% over 1 test(s)
- finish, copy: +5.9% over 1 test(s)
- finish, redesign: -12.1% over 1 test(s)
- home, notification: -0.6% over 1 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +0.5% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, hint: -3.5% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +7.0% over 1 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 76.1%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 69.3%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 21.2%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [adoption, new_flow] Express pet preset flow bypass: Provide preset pet choices directly on the pet pick screen to skip mandatory photo uploads. (why: Adoption has low conversion (69.3%) and a mean completion time of 1017s due to photo upload friction.)
1: [finish, new_screen] Pet control tutorial screen: Insert a dedicated tutorial screen before finishing onboarding explaining desktop controls and hiding features. (why: Support receives multiple inquiries regarding how to control, hide, or interact with pets after setup.)
2: [adoption, redesign] Pick friend grid layout overhaul: Redesign the companion selection screen into a grid layout for quick visual comparisons. (why: Adoption takes a long median time of 89s, showing friction in exploring available options.)
3: [adoption, copy] Clear photo upload tips: Add clear photo criteria copy to reduce custom pet generation errors. (why: Support received 3 emails about custom pet generation failing or looking wrong.)
4: [home, wait_info] Estimated generation time countdown: Display an estimated time remaining indicator on the pet generation wait screen. (why: Waiting step drops conversion to 81.3% with an extreme mean wait time of 2336s.)
5: [home, notification] Desktop notification when pet is ready: Trigger a desktop system notification when pet generation completes so users can switch back. (why: Mean wait time of 2336s indicates users leave the desktop app unattended while waiting.)
6: [adoption, layout] Compact adoption certificate layout: Change adoption certificate presentation to a compact card format. (why: Simplifying the certificate review stage reduces adoption step drop-off (69.3% conversion).)
7: [sign_in, copy] Sign-in data protection text: Clarify on the sign-in screen that creating an account saves pet profiles and prevents loss. (why: 8 support emails reported pets missing or reset after signing back in.)

scores.note: Bypassing photo upload friction with a new flow aligns with high-performing historical interventions.
Adding a mandatory tutorial screen introduces extra friction and risks dropping conversion.
Major redesigns historically hurt performance significantly.
Backed by support emails and cheap to implement, though copy updates yield minimal lift.
Wait time info updates showed negligible measured gain in past tests.
Notification changes previously yielded slight negative lift.
Layout adjustments showed no clear effect in prior iterations.
High support email evidence and config-only cost, but copy changes have modest overall impact.
